\looseness=-1 We identify conditioning-induced value overestimation (CIVO) as a systematic failure mode of temporal conditioning in imagination-based actor-critic training. Trained $\dt$-embeddings with multi-rate data exposure reliably induce value overestimation while frozen embeddings never do, revealing co-adaptation between the temporal embedding and the world model as the causal factor. The NVE diagnostic achieves perfect classification across all tested conditions (AUROC${=}1.000$, $n{=}36$). A four-level intervention hierarchy yields two key insights: gradient magnitude does not predict causal importance (the dominant pathway is causally inert while the weakest drives CIVO), and dual critics converge in pure imagination, rendering Double Q pessimism structurally ineffective in any system with shared imagined rollouts.

\looseness=-1 For practitioners, we recommend: (1)~validate with frozen-embedding controls before deploying learned embeddings; (2)~monitor NVE as an early warning; (3)~prefer MPC-style re-planning for variable-rate execution. tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{F6: $\dt{=}1$ imagination eliminates CIVO.}
Restricting imagination to $\dt{=}1$ while retaining the trained embedding (exp\_008e\_v3; Appendix~\ref{sec:code_corrections}) yields 0/4 CIVO (peak NVE ${\leq}0.8\times$); three seeds achieve $65$--$96\%$ of baseline (mean $775.6$; Figure~\ref{fig:multiple_pathways}). The trained embedding still receives gradients and develops $\dt$-conditioned representations, but since imagination exclusively queries $\dt{=}1$, the critic never encounters the biased $\dt{>}1$ predictions where reward fidelity degrades (\S\ref{sec:f2}). This localizes the vulnerability: the temporal embedding is necessary for co-adaptation, but the value amplification pathway requires $\dt{>}1$ rollouts to propagate bias into the critic. Multi-step imagination, not the trained embedding alone, is the necessary trigger for CIVO onset.

\looseness=-1 Full-SGS (exp\_018) detaches all non-KL gradients from $e_{\dt}$. \section{Why Standard Remedies Fail}
\label{sec:remedies}

The results of \S\ref{sec:results}--\ref{sec:f6} establish CIVO as a failure mode triggered by trained temporal embeddings with multi-rate exposure. We now ask: can standard RL remedies eliminate it? We evaluate seven interventions across four levels (Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}); none reliably succeeds across environments.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Intervention hierarchy. Prevention = peak NVE $< 2.0\times$ (35K+). Eval (\%BL) = mean${\pm}$std of final eval return as percentage of per-environment baseline (Walker 915.7, Cheetah 446.1). No level reliably eliminates CIVO across environments.
$^\dagger$Walker 2/4; Cheetah 1/1, PickCube 0/1.
$^\ddagger$Borderline (NVE${=}1.02\times$, eval 55\%).
$^\S$Policy erosion (final 15\% baseline).
$^\|$Walker 3/3, Cheetah 0/1.
$^\#$7 seeds, all NVE $< 2.0\times$.
$^\P$6 seeds, all NVE $< 2.0\times$.}
\label{tab:intervention_hierarchy}
\footnotesize
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Level} & \textbf{Intervention} & \textbf{Seeds} & \textbf{Prev.} & \textbf{Rate} & \textbf{Eval (\%BL)} \\
\midrule
--- & Untreated & 10 & 0/10 & 0\% & $15{\pm}10$ \\
\midrule
Gradient & Reward-only SGS & 2 & 0/2 & 0\% & $31{\pm}39$ \\

\midrule

\midrule

Repr. & TCN ($\sigma{=}0.5$) & 3 & 1/3 & 33\% & $20{\pm}11$ \\
Repr. & TCN ($\sigma{=}1.0$) & 1 & 1/1$^\S$ & 100\% & 16 \\
\midrule
Arch. & Wide single & 2 & 0/2 & 0\% & $39{\pm}8$ \\

\midrule

\paragraph{Gradient-level: magnitude does not predict causality.}
Full-SGS (exp\_018) detaches all non-KL gradients from $e_{\dt}$. Seed~1 shows partial mitigation (eval 448.3, NVE $1.66\times$) with late instability (NVE rising from $1.23\times$ mean to $1.66\times$ at 95K), suggesting SGS delays rather than prevents onset; seed~2 collapses entirely (peak ${\sim}488$ at 75K $\to$ 40.8 at 105K), indicating a metastable regime where stochastic factors determine whether delayed onset crosses the critical threshold (Appendix~\ref{sec:sgs_gradient_analysis}). Cross-environment validation on Cheetah confirms CIVO generalization (010b, NVE $8.27$--$108.52\times$); full-SGS yields 0/3 elimination. Removing the embedding eliminates CIVO on Cheetah (024b, NVE $< 0.2\times$). Targeted obs-decoder-only SGS (exp\_025/026) achieves 1/6 prevention (1/4 Walker, 0/2 Cheetah). Reward-only detachment (exp\_016e) produces NVE $10.42\times$---exceeding the untreated maximum ($4.72\times$; Table~\ref{tab:three_way_emb})---by amplifying the obs-decoder pathway (Appendix~\ref{sec:seed_divergence}). The pattern is consistent: blocking any single gradient channel shifts co-adaptation to the remaining ones, and the dominant gradient pathway (observation decoder) is causally inert while the weakest (KL) drives CIVO.

\paragraph{Output and representation levels: anchors drift and noise shows phase transitions.}
\textbf{RAVE} (value-level capping, $c \in \{1.5, 2.0\}$) fails because the EMA anchor tracks biased values during CIVO onset, rendering the clipping threshold permissive precisely when correction is needed (0/2 prevention, eval $6{\pm}4$\% of baseline). \textbf{TCN} (representation-level noise, $\sigma \in \{0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0\}$) shows binary on/off behavior: at $\sigma{=}0.2$, CIVO is suppressed in 2/4 Walker seeds while the remaining seeds escalate to full collapse with no intermediate outcome. The effective dose differs $5\times$ across environments ($\sigma{=}0.2$ partially effective on Walker; $\sigma{=}1.0$ erodes Cheetah policy to 15\% of baseline without preventing CIVO; Appendix~\ref{sec:tcn_cross_env}). This binary dose-response, combined with the absence of a smooth suppression curve, suggests a phase transition between co-adaptation regimes rather than a regularization effect amenable to hyperparameter tuning.

\paragraph{Architecture-level: pessimism vanishes in shared-data regimes.}
Dual critics converge across all tested configurations ($n{=}7$): correlation $\rho > 0.999$ with pessimism at only 3--4\% of the independent-critic bound, rendering standard pessimistic value estimation ineffective in pure imagination. The mechanism is structural: both critics train on the same imagined rollouts generated by the same world model, producing identical state-action distributions that drive convergence regardless of random initialization. A $2{\times}2$ factorial separates two components: narrow dual-critic (min, ${\sim}1.2$M) recovers from CIVO after onset (${\sim}16$--$19\times$ NVE ratio reduction) but does not prevent it; wide dual-critic (min $+$ ${\sim}2.4$M) achieves NVE $\leq 1.4\times$ in 3/4 seeds (3/3 Walker, 0/1 Cheetah), the sole positive result across all levels. Wide single (0/2) confirms both min-aggregation and increased capacity are necessary. Cross-environment transfer is limited: the single Cheetah seed (CIVO at $70\times$) exceeds the intervention's capacity, suggesting a severity ceiling (Appendix~\ref{sec:dual_critic_appendix}).

\paragraph{Unifying pattern: closed-loop imagination defeats single-pathway remedies.}
\label{sec:unifying}
The learned model generates both the training distribution and the bootstrap targets for critic updates; any remedy that assumes diverse or independent training sources---Double Q pessimism, EMA anchoring, noise injection---loses its corrective power when both sides of the training signal originate from the same model. Gradient interventions fail from pathway redundancy (blocking one channel amplifies another); output interventions fail from anchor co-drift (the anchor is corrupted by the same bias it should correct); representation interventions exhibit phase transitions (the embedding either co-adapts or does not, with no smooth intermediate); and pessimistic estimation fails from critic convergence (shared rollouts eliminate the diversity that pessimism requires). Only architectural changes that partially break the closed loop---wide dual-critic provides independent capacity that resists convergence---achieve partial prevention, and even this result does not transfer across environments.
